end.summary:
Practised visualising square and triangular numbers with dot pictures.
Explained that a growing square adds one row and one column, with the corner counted twice.
Used 13+13−1=25 to explain the difference between 12² and 13².
Explained the growth pattern and gave a picture-based reason for the repeated corner subtraction.
Teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised drawing and interpreting dot pictures for square and triangular numbers. They explained the new-row and new-column method, including why the shared corner is subtracted once, and used it to explain why 12² to 13² increases by 25. Drawing the full dot pictures independently still needs practice; at home, ask them to sketch 3², 4², and 1+2+3+4 and describe how each picture grows.
